drafted_by: AI, requires clinician review before any real use.

questions.text: What health problem are you concerned runs in your family: heart disease, cancer, diabetes, a genetic condition, mental illness, or something else?
questions.rationale: Clarifying which condition prompts the concern guides the next branch of the interview.

questions.text: Which relatives have had it: parents, brothers or sisters, children, grandparents, aunts or uncles? Is it on your mother's side, your father's side, or both?
questions.rationale: First-degree relatives and clustering on one side carry the most risk.

questions.text: About how old was each relative when they were diagnosed?
questions.rationale: Early age at diagnosis is a key marker of inherited risk.

questions.text: Are your parents living? If not, how old were they when they died and what was the cause?
questions.rationale: Parental age and cause of death frame the overall family risk.

questions.text: Has anyone in your family died suddenly or unexpectedly before age 50, such as drowning, a car crash with no clear cause, or dying in their sleep?
questions.rationale: Unexplained sudden death in a young relative raises concern for inherited heart rhythm or heart muscle disease.

questions.text: Has a close relative had a heart attack, stent, or bypass, especially a man before 55 or a woman before 65?
questions.rationale: Premature coronary disease in a first-degree relative raises cardiovascular risk.

questions.text: Has anyone been told they have a thickened or enlarged heart, a heart rhythm problem, or needed a pacemaker or defibrillator at a young age?
questions.rationale: Inherited cardiomyopathy and channelopathies warrant screening of relatives.

questions.text: Does anyone in your family have very high cholesterol or need cholesterol medicine at a young age?
questions.rationale: Very high cholesterol in young relatives suggests familial hypercholesterolemia.

questions.text: Has anyone had breast cancer, especially before 50 or in a man, or ovarian, pancreatic, or prostate cancer?
questions.rationale: These cancers cluster in BRCA and related hereditary syndromes.

questions.text: Has anyone had colon, rectal, or uterine cancer, especially before 50, or many colon polyps?
questions.rationale: Early colorectal or uterine cancer suggests Lynch syndrome or a polyposis syndrome.

questions.text: Have any relatives had other cancers, more than one cancer, or cancer in childhood?
questions.rationale: Multiple or unusual cancers in a family can indicate an inherited cancer syndrome.

questions.text: Has anyone in your family had genetic testing, and was a gene change found?
questions.rationale: A known familial variant allows targeted testing of the patient.

questions.text: Do your parents, brothers, or sisters have diabetes?
questions.rationale: First-degree family history raises the risk of type 2 diabetes.

questions.text: Has anyone had a stroke at a young age, a brain aneurysm, or bleeding in the brain?
questions.rationale: Two or more relatives with aneurysm can justify screening the patient.

questions.text: Has anyone had blood clots in the legs or lungs, especially without an obvious cause, or a known clotting disorder?
questions.rationale: Inherited thrombophilia changes risk with surgery, pregnancy, and hormones.

questions.text: Does anyone in your family bleed or bruise easily, or have hemophilia or another bleeding disorder?
questions.rationale: Inherited bleeding disorders matter before procedures or with heavy periods.

questions.text: Has anyone in your family had a serious or unexpected reaction to anesthesia, such as a very high fever during surgery?
questions.rationale: Malignant hyperthermia is inherited and must be known before any anesthetic.

questions.text: Does anyone have kidney disease, kidney cysts, or need dialysis?
questions.rationale: Polycystic kidney disease and other inherited nephropathies run in families.

questions.text: Has anyone had depression, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, addiction, or died by suicide?
questions.rationale: Family psychiatric and substance history raises the patient's own risk.

questions.text: Has anyone had dementia before 65, Huntington's disease, Parkinson's, or seizures?
questions.rationale: Early-onset neurodegenerative disease may be inherited.

questions.text: Do relatives have thyroid disease, celiac disease, lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, or other autoimmune conditions?
questions.rationale: Autoimmune conditions cluster in families.

questions.text: Are your parents related by blood, and what is your family's ancestry?
questions.rationale: Consanguinity and certain ancestries raise the risk of recessive conditions.

questions.text: Has anyone had birth defects, intellectual disability, or several pregnancy losses?
questions.rationale: These patterns suggest a chromosomal or single-gene condition.

questions.text: What is the main thing you are worried this could be?
questions.rationale: Understanding the patient's concern guides reassurance and follow-up questions.

red_flags.label: Sudden unexplained death in a young relative
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report a relative who died suddenly or unexpectedly before age 50, or fainted and died during exercise?

red_flags.label: Possible hereditary breast or ovarian cancer
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report breast cancer before 50, male breast cancer, ovarian cancer, or several relatives with breast, ovarian, pancreatic, or prostate cancer?

red_flags.label: Possible hereditary colon or uterine cancer
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report colon, rectal, or uterine cancer before 50, or several relatives with these cancers or many polyps?

red_flags.label: Family history of anesthesia reaction
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report a relative who had a dangerous reaction to anesthesia, such as a very high fever or muscle rigidity during surgery?

red_flags.label: Family history of brain aneurysm
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report one or more relatives with a brain aneurysm or bleeding in the brain?

red_flags.label: Inherited heart muscle or rhythm disease
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report relatives with cardiomyopathy, a heart rhythm disorder, or a defibrillator placed at a young age?
